3249-the-major.title: The Major
3249-the-major.creator: Ralph Connor
3249-the-major.description: A book by Ralph Connor. Upon the topmost tip of the taller of the twin poplars that flanked the picket gate opening upon the Gwynnes' little garden sat a robin, his head thrown back to give full throat to the song that was like to burst his heart, monotonous, unceasing, rapturous.

arxiv-2210-15863.title: Shape reconstructions by using plasmon resonances with enhanced sensitivity
arxiv-2210-15863.creator: Ming-Hui Ding, Hongyu Liu, Guang-Hui Zheng
arxiv-2210-15863.description: Abstract ABSTRACT This paper investigates the shape reconstructions of sub-wavelength objects from near-field measurements in transverse electromagnetic scattering. This geometric inverse problem is notoriously ill-posed and challenging. We develop a novel reconstruction scheme using plasmon resonances with significantly enhanced sensitivity and resolution.

arxiv-2303-09135.title: Regret, Delete, (Do Not) Repeat: An Analysis of Self-Cleaning Practices on Twitter After the Outbreak of the COVID-19 Pandemic Conference: Extended Abstracts of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 23–28, 2023; Hamburg, Germany Extended Abstracts of the 2023 CHI Confe
arxiv-2303-09135.creator: Nicolás E. Díaz Ferreyra, Gautam Kishore Shahi, Catherine Tony, Stefan Stieglitz, Riccardo Scandariato
arxiv-2303-09135.description: Abstract . During the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, many people shared their symptoms across Online Social Networks (OSNs) like Twitter, hoping for others’ advice or moral support. Prior studies have shown that those who disclose health-related information across OSNs often tend to regret it and delete their publications afterwards.

arxiv-2402-01454.description: Abstract In practical statistical causal discovery (SCD), embedding domain expert knowledge as constraints into the algorithm is important for reasonable causal models reflecting the broad knowledge of domain experts , despite the challenges in the systematic acquisition of background knowledge.

arxiv-2406-18531.creator: Duy Duong-Tran, Nghi Nguyen, Shizhuo Mu, Jiong Chen, Jingxuan Bao, Frederick Xu, Sumita Garai, Jose Cadena-Pico, Alan David Kaplan, Tianlong Chen, Yize Zhao, Li Shen, Joaquín Goñi
arxiv-2406-18531.description: Abstract In systems and network neuroscience, many common practices in brain connectomic analysis are often not properly scrutinized. One such practice is mapping a predetermined set of sub-circuits, like functional networks (FNs), onto subjects’ functional connectomes (FCs) without adequately assessing the information-theoretic appropriateness of the partition.

arxiv-2504-02838.title: Matrix encoding method in variational quantum singular value decomposition
arxiv-2504-02838.creator: Alexander I. Zenchuk, Wentao Qi, Junde Wu
arxiv-2504-02838.description: Abstract We propose the variational quantum singular value decomposition based on encoding the elements of the considered N × N N\times N matrix into the state of a quantum system of appropriate dimension. This method doesn’t use the expansion of this matrix in terms of the unitary matrices. Controlled measurement is involved to avoid small success probability in ancilla measurement.

pmc-11440995.title: Utilizing MRI, [18F]FDG-PET and [89Zr]Zr-DFO-28H1 FAP-PET tracer to assess inflammation and fibrogenesis in a reproducible lung injury rat model: a multimodal imaging study
pmc-11440995.creator: Milou Boswinkel, René Raavé, Andor Veltien, Tom WJ Scheenen, Nina Fransén Petterson, René in ‘t Zandt, Lars E. Olsson, Karin von Wachenfeldt, Sandra Heskamp, Irma Mahmutovic Persson
pmc-11440995.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). ObjectiveAccurate imaging biomarkers that indicate disease progression at an early stage are highly important to enable timely mitigation of symptoms in progressive lung disease. In this context, reproducible experimental models and readouts are key. Here, we aim to show reproducibility of a lung injury rat model by inducing disease and assessing disease progression by multi-modal non-invasive imaging techniques at two different research sites.

pmc-11509609.description: Background and Objectives: Traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) is a devastating condition that occurs in two phases: primary and secondary injury. These phases contribute to changes in blood vessels and the influx of inflammatory cells such as neutrophils and lymphocytes.

pmc-12625869.title: COVID-19 antibody testing study: a nested substudy within Alberta’s Tomorrow Project (ATP) in Alberta, Canada
pmc-12625869.creator: Sara Nejatinamini, Carmen Charlton, Shandra Harman, Jamil N Kanji, James D Kellner, Kristyn Lines, Kathleen Murdoch, Wendy Powell, Joseph Roberts, Will Rosner, Grace Shen-Tu, Graham Tipples, Jian-Yi Xu, Jennifer E Vena
pmc-12625869.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeThe Alberta’s Tomorrow Project (ATP) prospective cohort study was established in 2000 to investigate the causes of cancer and chronic disease. The cohort consists of almost 55 000 participants aged 35–69 years at the time of recruitment. From 2020 to 2022, ATP conducted a longitudinal substudy, the COVID-19 Antibody Testing (CAT) study, nested in this existing cohort, to understand the spread and impact of the SARS-CoV-2.

pmc-13114739.title: Lattice Radiation Therapy Plays a Synergistic Role in the Radical Treatment of Bulky Cervical Cancer: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-13114739.creator: Feifei Wang, Qianru Zhan, Zhitao Dai, Huijuan Zhang, Miao Peng, Zhijian Chen, Jing Jin, Xiugui Sheng
pmc-13114739.description: Simple SummaryBulky cervical cancer is extremely challenging to treat with traditional methods. Lattice radiation therapy was previously used primarily for palliation. We reported that lattice radiation therapy plays a synergistic role in the radical treatment of locally advanced bulky cervical cancer, with only manageable grade IV hematological toxicity observed.
